title: Swap through pointers
hints: `a` and `b` are addresses. `*a` is the caller's variable itself: reading it gives the value, assigning to it changes the caller's variable.
A tuple assignment evaluates the whole right side first: `*a, *b = *b, *a` swaps without a temporary.
In `SwapIfGreater`, return `false` early when `*a <= *b`; otherwise call `Swap(a, b)` (no `&`: they are already pointers) and return `true`.
